questions.explanation: 'Would' marks the past habit; 'used to' would also work, but 'will' cannot describe the past.
questions.q: As a student, he ___ cycle ten miles to lectures.

questions.explanation: Formal obligation in regulations uses 'shall', not the weaker 'should'.
Fronted 'seldom' requires inversion of the auxiliary and subject.

questions.q: Choose the sentence emphasising THE INTERN.
options: It was the intern which discovered the flaw.
It was the intern when discovered the flaw.
It was the intern that place discovered the flaw.
It was the intern who discovered the flaw.
questions.explanation: The it-cleft focuses the agent: 'It was the intern who', not 'which'.
The absolute phrase needs its own subject + participle: 'the vote having been counted'.
After 'demand', the mandative subjunctive uses the base form 'be'.
'Only if' fronted inverts the main clause: 'will we'.
options: Only if you sign we will
Only if you sign will we
Only if you signed we would
Only if sign you will we
If I would have known, I would have acted.
Had I would know, I would have acted.
If had I known, I would have acted.
Had I known, I would have acted.
questions.explanation: 'Had' inverts with the subject in formal unreal past conditionals.
Nominalisation packs the process into a dense noun phrase: 'the erosion of'.
'Suggests' hedges the claim; 'proves' overstates the evidence.
questions.q: The data ___ a link between the variables.

questions.explanation: The fixed idiom is 'by and large', meaning 'on the whole'.

options: A truth is stranger than fiction.
The truth is stranger than fiction.
Some truth is stranger than fiction.
questions.explanation: Abstract 'truth' in a general maxim takes the zero article.
'Whereby' means 'by which', introducing the mechanism.
'Is believed to have' + past participle reports a past rumour formally.
Emphatic 'did' + base verb contradicts the denial.

options: He agreed, although it was unwillingly.
He agreed, albeit it was unwillingly.
questions.explanation: 'Albeit' + adjective phrase concedes without a full clause.
'Object to' takes a gerund because 'to' is a preposition here.
'Commence' is the formal register equivalent of 'start'.
Fronted 'down' with 'came' inverts dramatically: 'Down came'.

options: Much I respect him as, I must disagree.
Much as respect I him, I must disagree.
As much I respect him, I must disagree.
Much as I respect him, I must disagree.
questions.explanation: 'Much as' + clause concedes before the contrasting main statement.
